  • Why does my Carplay encounter frequent disconnection after using for months?

    1.The plugs of these wires are loose or pulled too tight, resulting in poor contact . 2.Because of the internal instability of Mazda system. Please update your OS version to above 74.00.021 N AN/ F AN. ThIS version will be more stable.

  • Do the Carplay Kit fits 2018 Maxda CX-5?

    Yes,it fits Maxda CX-5 2015 -2020.

  • Why does my Mazda carplay cannot work?

    1.Pls check your carplay is update to 70.00.01 or above. 2.Please check whether the Siri is opened when connecting. 3.Check whether it is caused by the connection line does not touch well! 4.Make sure that your car have MZD connection device

  • Why dos the GPS or navigation cannot work properly?

    Before upgrading the firmware, you should remove the SD card and insert it when you complete the upgrade in case the navigation cannot work.

  • If the carplay have worked for several months and failed,what should I do ?

    You try to restore the carplay to Factory setting or send message to us.

    Transforming Mazda 3 into a Smart Tech Hub

    Reviewed in the United States on January 15, 2024

    The Dasbecan Apple Carplay Android Auto Retrofit Kit is not just an upgrade; it's a revolution for your Mazda 3 driving experience. This kit seamlessly brings the cutting-edge connectivity and convenience of Apple Carplay and Android Auto into the cockpit of your Mazda 3. It's like giving your car a brain transplant, upgrading it from a regular vehicle to a smart, connected companion.

    The installation process is a key highlight. Designed with the Mazda 3 in mind, the retrofit kit fits like a glove. It's a relief to find an aftermarket product that meshes so well with the existing system. The integration is so smooth, it feels like these features were always meant to be part of your car. For those who are not mechanically inclined, a professional installation is a good idea to ensure everything is up and running perfectly.

    Once installed, the functionality is a game-changer. The system brings the familiar interface of your smartphone to your car's dashboard. Whether you're an iPhone devotee or an Android aficionado, this kit bridges the gap between your phone and your car. Maps, music, messages, and more are all at your fingertips, or better yet, a voice command away. It's a seamless transition from your digital life outside the car to inside.

    The user experience is smooth and intuitive. The response is snappy, and the interface is user-friendly. It's like your car's infotainment system got an upgrade to first-class, with all the modern conveniences you could ask for. The integration with existing controls and the touch screen enhances the overall driving experience, keeping you connected without being distracting.

    The quality of the components in the kit is top-notch. Everything feels well-made and durable, which is reassuring when you're modifying such an essential part of your car. The attention to detail in design and manufacturing means that this retrofit kit doesn't just add functionality; it also adds value to your vehicle.

    TL;DR: The Dasbecan Retrofit Kit is a must-have for Mazda 3 owners looking to modernize their ride. It brings the ease and functionality of Apple Carplay and Android Auto into your car with a seamless, integrated experience. The kit not only enhances your driving experience but also adds value to your vehicle with its high-quality components and intuitive design.

    Until someone offers an aftermarket head unit this is what you need for AA/CP in a Mazda.

    Reviewed in the United States on June 15, 2023
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    If you didn't get Android Auto or Apple CarPlay when you purchased your late model Mazda, this is what you need for OEM integration... for a FRACTION of the price from the dealer. This worked great in my '19 MX-5 Miata Club. As others mentioned, I updated the firmware per instructions found on the web and YouTube. This takes about 40 minutes. Luckily the interior panels of the Miata come apart pretty easily and it only took about 30 min for the physical install of the hardware. This will no doubt take longer if you have no experience in pulling automotive interior panels. BTW, for the ND Miata, while you're in there you might as well change out the cabin air filter. This kit came with foam tape for sound deadening, two LONG cables, zip ties and an instruction manual. No, it's not wireless and it's not the perfect integration of AA/CP, but it's inexpensive and it's what we've got until someone develops an aftermarket head until to fit the form factor and functionality of our cars.

  • TobycW
    5 out of 5 stars
    Verified Purchase

    Great

    Reviewed in the United States on October 2, 2023
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    A video on youtube had a link to this product. Not sure what the differences are between so many similar. This product ended up great. Quality looks very good. Had a thorough manual and OE looking cables and module. Had a bunch of zip ties and foam included. Once installed in my 2017 MX-5, everything worked perfectly. Had full use of the steering wheel buttons and center console buttons. I am not sure but I think Mazda locks out the touch screen when in motion.

    Install on an MX-5: I did not remove the shifter console! It took about 45 minutes in all. Follow the youtube video to get to the cmu. Then do the following: For the USB module, remove the passenger side center console side trim in the footwell. Remove the "H" looking trim to the sides of the USB module. Remove the Seat heater controls/airbag lights module above the USB module. From the side where you removed the passenger console trim, you should see top and bottom clips of the USB module you want to remove. Take a long but small flat head screw driver and one-by-one break the clips. It should be easy to push it out from behind now. Saved me so much time doing it this way and I hope it does for you too! Remember, all trim is held in by clips or fits like a jigsaw puzzle. NEVER force anything. A nudge and a pull should be all that it takes. I broke nothing on mine installing it. There are a couple of good youtube videos for the MX-5 that you can look at before you start.

    Worked great for 3 months

    Reviewed in the United States on March 23, 2024
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    Ordered and installed this unit on 8/1/23. In my 2017 Mazda6 Grand Touring.

    Installation was pretty easy. As long as you are comfortable with carefully removing dash trim pieces and routing cables through your dash and console. The unit included foam padding to secure around the cabling to prevent chafing and rattling. Everything was included to perform a clean install if you take your time and consider the best paths to route and secure the cables.

    Make sure you check your vehicles firmware version prior to ordering. A firmware update can be intimidating and could possibly brick your car’s infotainment system if not done properly. Luckily mine was already several versions above the required version and didn’t require an update for this inst.

    11/12/23 started experiencing issues with car play disconnecting and reconnecting randomly while driving. I figured it was my cord so I ordered a new Apple certified cord. I immediately had the same problem with my new cord. I then tried my daughters iPhone with the new cord and had the same result. It’s frustrating but usually would connect and keep a connection to car play for a while when driving before occurring again.

    1/7/24 Apple car play no longer works with this device. Ive tried multiple Apple certified cables that work with car play in my other vehicles. This device no longer operates at all. I’ve opened up my dash and console again and have ensured all cable connections are tight. I can plug in my iPhone and it will charge but Apple car play will not connect and be displayed on my screen.

    3/22/24 it’s been a couple months without car play now. I’m frustrated and disappointed in this device as it worked well when first installed. I’m now looking for a similar device with better quality. At this time I would NOT purchase this product again or recommend anyone else purchase one as I did when I first installed it. Disappointed enough to write this review as I’m out the cost of this unit and hours of my time installing this device and then opening back up my dash and console to troubleshoot and inspect connections.

    I’ve seen comments from other people who’ve purchased and installed this device around the same time frame with the same exact issue. Calling out a faulty unit after only a few months. If it is a faulty unit, I would hope the manufacturer or seller would

    be willing to replace the unit. I’m an electronics engineer who also has a background in mechanics I would be more than happy to send you back my faulty unit for failure analysis.

    Great concept but poor quality. A device of this sort should not start failing within 90 days of use in an automotive setting where it only gets maybe a couple hours of use each day. A total failure within 5 months of use is simply unacceptable for a product of this nature.

    It works

    Reviewed in the United States on January 30, 2023
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    So far I’m not happy with this purchase. It took me nearly three hours to install (granted I’m a bit obsessive when it comes to my car), but almost immediately I started having issues. It works maybe half of the time. The primary issue being the message “No CarPlay device detected.” This is curious because if I don’t plug in my phone, no message appears. When it does work it’s frequently slow/freezes for a moment or two, and twice now has blacked out the screen on the car until I shut the car off.

    Needless to say, I’m very frustrated at this point.

    I’m in the process of troubleshooting and will update accordingly. I have service scheduled at the dealership to update the firmware. In the meantime I’m going to test with other devices (another iPhone and an Android) to try and determine if the issue is the hub (you know, what I’m reviewing), the car, or the phone.

    UPDATE: The installed firmware was the earliest possible firmware that was compatible with this hub. After taking the car to the dealership for an update, the hub now works better than it had.

    It’s far from perfect though I think it might be my phone that takes the blame. While lightening cables are not directional, it doesn’t always connect when plugging it in to the car. Sometimes I need to unplug the cord, rotate it 180° then plug it back in, which is frustrating. It’s also quite slow, but I suspect that’s more of a Mazda issue.

    All in all, I’m just happy to have CarPlay in my car. This is much cheaper than OEM, so if you’re trying to save some money, this is the part for you.
